title: Fort Lauderdale Seawall Height Requirement
question: How high does a seawall have to be in Fort Lauderdale?
unit: ft NAVD88, capped at BFE or 6.0
qualifier: Fort Lauderdale sets both ends. The minimum is 5 ft NAVD88 and the maximum is your base flood elevation or 6 ft NAVD88, whichever is lower - and where those two rules collide, the minimum wins. The city also runs a waiver nobody mentions, which expires the day you sell. The barrier is designed against tidal flooding through the year 2070.
detail_rows: Minimum :: 5 ft NAVD88 for a new or modified tidal flood barrier. ULDR 47-19.13.D(1). | Maximum :: The base flood elevation on the FEMA FIRM, or 6 ft NAVD88, whichever is lower. In an X zone the cap is the natural ground elevation. Where the maximum would conflict with the 5 ft minimum, the minimum governs. ULDR 47-19.13.D(12). | The 2035 route :: An application before 1 January 2035 may be permitted at 4 ft NAVD88, provided the barrier is designed to accommodate 5 ft NAVD88 by 1 January 2050. ULDR 47-19.13.D(1). | The waiver most people never hear about :: If the principal structure has a habitable finished floor below 4.0 ft NAVD88, the city engineer may waive the minimum. It runs three years at most, it becomes void the moment the property changes hands, and the city can rescind it on fifteen days' notice if the wall is overtopped or fails to perform. The request fee is $186. | The 3.9 figure is dead :: Before 23 March 2023 the minimum was 3.9 ft NAVD88 for properties with a base flood elevation of 4.0 ft, with a 5.0 ft maximum. Ordinance C-23-05 deleted it. Many existing walls were built to it, so an older wall that met code when it went in can now sit below the current minimum. | What counts as substantial :: Either test triggers it - work along more than 50% of the shoreline length, or work exceeding 50% of the fair market replacement cost of the existing structure. Note it is replacement cost of the structure, not property value. ULDR 47-19.13.C(12). | The trap in that definition :: Docks, finger piers, piles and ancillary footers are excluded from the calculation - but a concrete dock poured monolithically with the seawall cap is counted in. | The whole shoreline :: A barrier undergoing substantial repair must be built along the property's entire shoreline. ULDR 47-19.13.D(7). To the extent practicable it must also adjoin the neighbours' barriers to close gaps. D(6). | The clock, and it is a citable offence :: 60 days to show progress after a citation, 365 days to complete. Letting tidal water trespass onto a neighbour or the right-of-way is declared a public nuisance. A wall built to the standard that is simply overtopped is not. ULDR 47-19.13.D(2) and (3). | What it costs to ignore :: Up to $500 per violation, and each day a violation continues is a separate offence. Code of Ordinances Sec. 1-6(c). The city may also repair a seawall itself and place a lien for the cost. Sec. 2-155(2). | Riprap on new walls :: A vertical seawall built in marine waters where none existed before must carry natural limerock riprap, or approved habitat enhancement, at the waterward face. ULDR 47-19.13.D(8). Riprap on its own does not count as a barrier. C(13). | Caps :: A cap added to an existing wall must be at least as wide as the existing cap. D(5). | Your dock follows the wall :: On a new or reconstructed barrier a dock may sit up to 12 inches above the maximum elevation allowed. On an existing structure, up to 12 inches above that structure's top. ULDR 47-19.3(f). | Disclosure when you sell :: Contracts executed after 23 March 2023 for property in a tidally influenced area must carry a tidal flood barrier disclosure in capitalised bold-faced type of at least 14 point. ULDR 47-19.13.E. | Where it does not apply :: Oceanfront beaches and shorelines seaward of the Coastal Construction Control Line. ULDR 47-19.13.B. | Permits :: Development Services, through the LauderBuild portal. Signed and sealed plans for the seawall and piles by a Florida licensed engineer or architect, a special inspector form for pile installation, and dredge approval from Broward County and/or FDEP. The single-family engineering permit fee is $244, adjusted annually for CPI without a hearing. Code Sec. 9-54.
source: City of Fort Lauderdale ULDR Sec. 47-19.13, Resiliency Standards for Tidal Flood Protection (Ord. C-23-05, 23 March 2023) and Sec. 47-19.3(f); Code of Ordinances Secs. 1-6, 2-155 and 9-54; Broward County Code Ch. 39, Art. XXV, Sec. 39-407

title: Seawall Permits in Fort Lauderdale
question: Do I need a permit to repair a seawall in Fort Lauderdale?
unit: city permit + county license
qualifier: Yes. Fort Lauderdale requires a permit from its Development Services Department before work on mooring structures, a term its code defines to include seawalls. A substantial repair (more than half the shoreline, or over half the wall's fair market replacement cost) must meet the city's tidal flood barrier height, which is also capped at the FEMA base flood elevation or 6 ft NAVD88. Broward County also requires its own Environmental Resource License, often a general license for a repair in the same place.
detail_rows: City :: A permit from the Development Services Department is required before construction of mooring structures, defined to include a seawall; on navigable waters every regulating authority must also approve, and the applicant certifies ownership of the abutting land or produces the owner's written consent - Code Sec. 8-91(a)(2), (b). The city's Permitting Services FAQ lists seawalls among permits filed with a copy of a current survey and a completed Zoning Affidavit, and a permit renewed before it expires costs 50% of the original fee (100% after expiry). Substantial repair = work along more than 50% of the property's shoreline or over 50% of the wall's fair market replacement cost; docks, finger piers and piles are not counted - ULDR Sec. 47-19.13.C.12. Such walls need 5.0 ft NAVD88 (4.0 ft for applications before 1 Jan 2035 if designed to reach 5.0 ft by 2050), must run along the entire shoreline, and may not top the FEMA base flood elevation or 6 ft NAVD88, whichever is lower - Sec. 47-19.13.D.1, D.7, D.12. The city engineer may grant a waiver of up to 3 years where the home's habitable floor is below 4.0 ft NAVD88 - Sec. 47-19.13.D.1 (Ord. C-23-05) | Broward County :: Construction in regulated aquatic resources needs a county Environmental Resource License (ERL) - Broward County Code Sec. 27-333(a)(1). Repairing an existing functional seawall no more than 1 ft waterward of its authorized location, or a new wall within 1 ft of the old wet face with the old wall left in place, qualifies for a general license (Sec. 27-336(a)(1)b.), as do refacing, crack filling, seepage holes and other minor repairs (n.) and raising the cap in the same footprint (o.); the code says a general license is issued within 10 days of a complete application - Sec. 27-336(a)(1) | State :: Restoring a seawall at its previous location, upland of it, or within 18 inches waterward is exempt from a state environmental resource permit; the exemption does not replace permission to use state-owned submerged land or county and city requirements, and does not cover chapter 161 coastal permits - s. 403.813(1), (1)(e), F.S. | Federal :: A U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (Department of the Army) authorization is required for structures or work in or affecting navigable waters, unless exempt or covered by a nationwide or regional general permit - 33 CFR 322.3(a) (Rivers and Harbors Act s. 10)
source: Fort Lauderdale Code Sec. 8-91; ULDR Sec. 47-19.13 (Supp. 58); Permitting Services page; Broward County Code Ch. 27 Art. XI Secs. 27-333, 27-336 (Supp. 72); s. 403.813(1)(e), F.S. (2026); 33 CFR 322.3(a)

title: Fort Lauderdale Flood Zone & Elevation Rules
question: What flood zone is Fort Lauderdale in, and what does it require?
unit: lowest floor above base flood elevation; no extra city freeboard
qualifier: Fort Lauderdale's floodplain chapter adds no freeboard number of its own for ordinary buildings, so the Florida Building Code's BFE + 1 ft applies. What the city does add is a two-year look-back: improvements are added up over two years when testing the 50% substantial-improvement line.
detail_rows: City freeboard :: None set for ordinary buildings in Code Ch. 14; critical facilities must be at BFE + 3 ft or the 500-year flood elevation, whichever is higher - Sec. 14-11. | Substantial improvement :: Any combination of work taking place during a two-year period whose cumulative cost equals or exceeds 50% of the building's market value - Sec. 14-1. | City lookup tool :: The city's flood-insurance page sends owners to its GIS Application (gis.fortlauderdale.gov/FemaFloodZones) to read the FIRM zone for a parcel; the same page still quotes 2014 maps and a 20% discount, which FEMA's current records supersede. | FEMA flood map :: FEMA's Community Status Book (report dated 3 Oct 2026) lists Fort Lauderdale as NFIP community 125105 with a current effective FIRM dated 31 Jul 2024. Zones are set parcel by parcel, so no single zone covers the whole city - check your own address. | NFIP history :: FEMA record: first flood hazard boundary map 3 Nov 1972; first FIRM 3 Nov 1972; regular NFIP program since 3 Nov 1972; entered CRS 1 Oct 1992. | Flood insurance discount :: CRS class 7 - 15% off NFIP premiums for policies in the Special Flood Hazard Area (class in effect 1 Oct 2020). | State minimum :: 2023 Florida Building Code, Residential R322.2.1 and R322.3.2 - lowest floor (A zones) or bottom of the lowest horizontal structural member (V and Coastal A zones) at BFE + 1 ft or the design flood elevation, whichever is higher. | Look up your zone :: City GIS Application (gis.fortlauderdale.gov/FemaFloodZones) or FEMA's Flood Map Service Center (msc.fema.gov), the official public source for FIRMs.
source: Fort Lauderdale Code of Ordinances Ch. 14 Secs. 14-1, 14-11; City of Fort Lauderdale Flood - Flood Insurance page; FEMA Community Status Book, Florida (www.fema.gov/cis/FL.html, report 10/03/2026); 2023 Florida Building Code, Residential R322.2.1, R322.3.2; 44 CFR 59.1; FEMA Flood Map Service Center

title: Dock Permits & Size Limits in Fort Lauderdale
question: How big a dock can I build in Fort Lauderdale?
unit: whichever is less, from the property line
qualifier: Fort Lauderdale caps a dock at 25% of the waterway's width or 25 ft from the property line, whichever is less. Mooring piles may reach 30% or 25 ft, and the boat itself must stay inside the house's side setback lines extended into the water. Only the City Commission can go further, and never past 30% of the width.
detail_rows: Dock projection :: Docks, slips, davits, hoists and similar mooring structures may not extend into the waterway more than 25% of its width or 25 ft, whichever is less, measured from the property line. A principal building must already exist on the lot - ULDR 47-19.3(c) | Mooring and dolphin piles :: No more than 30% of the waterway width or 25 ft beyond the property line, whichever is less - 47-19.3(d) | Commission waiver :: The City Commission may waive (c) and (d) in extraordinary circumstances after a public hearing with notice to owners within 300 ft, but never beyond 30% of the waterway width; no Board of Adjustment variance can go past 30%. Piles beyond (d) need 5-inch marine reflector tape in international orange or iridescent silver within 18 inches of the top - 47-19.3(e) | Deck height :: A dock installed after 23 March 2023 may not sit higher than the maximum tidal flood barrier elevation at that spot; up to 12 inches higher if attached to a new or rebuilt barrier, not poured monolithically with the cap and not blocking water flow over it - 47-19.3(f) | Boat position :: No watercraft docked beside residential property may extend beyond the side setback lines required for the principal building, extended into the waterway. Isle of Venice and Hendricks Isle owners are excepted under Resolution 85-270 - 47-19.3(h),(i) | Lifts and davits :: One mooring device per first 100 ft of lot width (a second on 100-200 ft lots needs Site Plan Level II review) plus one PWC lift; cross-section no more than 1 sq ft, height no more than 6.5 ft above lot grade; a hoisted boat's lowest point no more than 1 ft above the seawall cap - 47-19.3(b) | No boathouses :: No boathouse or boat cover in the required setback or over a public waterway - 47-19.3(g) | Melrose Park and Riverland Road :: In these annexed areas docks may project only 5 ft beyond the property line or bulkhead line and must stay 10 ft from the neighbour's plot line, except in RS-6.85B and RD-12.22 where 47-19.3 applies - ULDR 47-39.A.1.b(12)(a),(i) | Permit :: A permit from the development services department, plus approval of every agency regulating navigable waters; the applicant must own the upland or have the owner's written consent - Code Sec. 8-91(b) | Moored boats :: Code Sec. 8-91(e) separately limits moored boats to 30% of the canal or waterway width from the recorded property line | Broward County license :: Work in the county's regulated aquatic resources, which include canals and tidal waters, needs a Broward County Environmental Resource License - County Code 27-332, 27-333(a)(1). A new dock, floating dock or other over-water structure of 500 sq ft or less, measured from the seawall's wet face at mean high water, with no dredging or filling beyond the pilings, qualifies for a general license issued within 10 days of a complete application - 27-336(a)(1)e. A county ordinance that sets minimum environmental-protection standards prevails over city ordinances - Broward County Charter Sec. 11.01 | State exemption :: A private, non-commercial dock on pilings with 1,000 sq ft or less of over-water surface (500 sq ft in Outstanding Florida Waters), and the only exempt dock along 65 ft of shoreline (or one per lot if the lot is narrower), needs no state environmental permit - Fla. Stat. 403.813(1)(b). The exemption does not grant permission to use state-owned submerged lands and does not override city or county rules - 403.813(1) | Federal :: Structures in navigable waters need a Department of the Army permit, general or individual - 33 CFR 322.3(a)
source: Fort Lauderdale ULDR Sec. 47-19.3 (through Ord. C-26-03, 1-20-26) and 47-39.A.1.b(12); Code of Ordinances Sec. 8-91 (through Ord. C-23-13); Broward County Code Secs. 27-332, 27-333, 27-336 (through Ord. 2026-16); Broward County Charter Sec. 11.01; Fla. Stat. 403.813(1)(b) (2026); 33 CFR 322.3(a)

title: Boat Lift Rules in Fort Lauderdale
question: What are the boat lift rules in Fort Lauderdale?
headline_answer: Allowed, one per 100 ft of lot width
unit: mooring device + 1 PWC lift; 6.5 ft max height
qualifier: Fort Lauderdale lets you put davits, hoists and boat lifts on a seawall or dock, but counts them: one mooring device for each 100 feet of lot width, plus one lift used only for a personal watercraft. The device itself is capped at 6.5 feet above lot grade with a one-square-foot cross section, and a raised boat's lowest point may sit no more than one foot above the seawall cap. A permit from Development Services comes first.
detail_rows: Allowed where :: Boat davits, hoists and similar mooring devices may be erected on a seawall or dock - ULDR Sec. 47-19.3(b). Mooring devices are defined to include boat davits, hoists and boat lifts - Sec. 47-19.3(a)(1) | How many :: One mooring device for the first 100 feet of lot width or portion of it, and one for each additional 100 feet. A second device on a lot wider than 100 but under 200 feet needs Site Plan Level II approval by the development review committee, which looks at neighbours' views and the device's height, width and length - Sec. 47-19.3(b)(1) | Jet ski lift :: In addition, one lift designed and used solely for a personal watercraft is allowed per development site - Sec. 47-19.3(b)(2) | Size and height :: The davit, hoist or other device may not exceed one square foot in cross section or 6.5 feet above lot grade - Sec. 47-19.3(b)(3) | Boat when raised :: The lowest appendage of the vessel may not be hoisted more than one foot above the seawall cap, or above average grade where there is no seawall - Sec. 47-19.3(b)(4) | Covers :: No boathouse, permanent covering or temporary covering for a boat is allowed within the zoning setback area, and none may be placed over a public waterway - Sec. 47-19.3(g) | Projection :: The code sets no separate reach for the lift itself; it goes on the seawall or dock, and docks and similar mooring structures may extend 25% of the waterway width or 25 feet, whichever is less, from the property line. Moored boats may extend up to 30% of the canal width - Sec. 47-19.3(c); Code Sec. 8-91(e) | Principal building first :: Davits, hoists and similar mooring structures may only be built on a lot that already has a principal building and abuts a waterway - Sec. 47-19.3(c) | Permit :: A permit from the Development Services Department is required before erecting boat davits, hoists or similar mooring structures; on navigable waters every regulating agency must also approve, and the applicant must own the waterfront land or have the owner's written consent - Code Sec. 8-91(b) | Guide pole :: Any part of a lift that can be submerged needs a vertical guide pole at least 1.5 inches in diameter, standing at least 6 feet above the water at all times, with a reflective finish - Code Sec. 8-91(d) | Melrose Park and Riverland Road :: In these annexed areas a boat lift may not exceed 15 feet in height, must stay 10 feet from side plot lines and may extend no more than 33% of the waterway or 25 feet; lifts more than 5 feet out need night reflectors - ULDR Sec. 47-39.A.1.b(11) | Broward County :: Boatlifts and davits are listed among the projects that qualify for a county general environmental resource license, which the code says is issued within ten days of a complete application - Broward County Code Sec. 27-336(a)(1)f. | State and federal :: Floating boat lifts and floating vessel platforms that meet s. 403.813(1)(s), F.S. (they float at all times, hold the vessel out of the water, and either sit inside a previously permitted slip or total no more than 500 sq ft - 200 sq ft in Outstanding Florida Waters - beside a qualifying dock or bulkhead) need no state permit; a local government may then ask only for a one-time registration unless the platform is attached to a bulkhead with no dock. Structures in navigable waters otherwise need Army Corps authorization unless exempt or under a general permit - 33 CFR 322.3(a).
source: City of Fort Lauderdale ULDR Sec. 47-19.3 and 47-39.A.1.b(11) (Supp. 58 Update 2) and Code of Ordinances Sec. 8-91 (Supp. 67 Update 2); Broward County Code Sec. 27-336 (Supp. 72); s. 403.813(1)(s), F.S. (2026); 33 CFR 322.3(a)

title: Waterfront Deck Rules in Fort Lauderdale
question: What are the deck setback and railing rules in Fort Lauderdale?
unit: from the waterway for shade structures, screen enclosures and tall planters; decks per height
qualifier: Fort Lauderdale measures every waterway yard from the wet face of the seawall. A deck at or below the ground-floor level needs no setback at all, a raised deck must stay 5 ft from property lines and no more than 2.5 ft above the finished floor, and gazebos, tiki huts, trellises and pool screen enclosures must stay 10 ft back from the water.
detail_rows: Where the yard is measured :: A yard along a waterway is measured from the face of the seawall in contact with the water (the wet face), or from the edge of the waterway where there is no seawall. ULDR Sec. 47-2.2.S. | At-grade decks :: Allowed in front, rear and side yards with no required setback, but not higher than the finished floor elevation of the ground floor. ULDR Sec. 47-19.2.G.1. | Above-grade decks :: Allowed in required yards no closer than 5 ft to any property line and no more than 2.5 ft above the ground-floor finished floor elevation; a visible vertical edge must be finished to match the deck. Sec. 47-19.2.G.2. | Gazebos, tiki huts, trellises :: In the rear yard, 10 ft from the waterway; open on all sides, max 12 ft tall, max 200 sq ft in the yard, one per plot. Sec. 47-19.2.P. | Pools and screen enclosures :: Single-family pools 5 ft from any property line and not above the ground-floor finished floor; setback measured from the outer edge of coping. Screen enclosures 10 ft from a property line abutting a waterway, max 12 ft tall in the rear yard, and no more than 5% of required pervious area may sit inside them. Sec. 47-19.2.BB. | Planters :: On a waterway, planters taller than 2.5 ft above grade stay 10 ft from the waterway. Sec. 47-19.2. | Sheds and tanks :: Utility sheds on a waterway lot must meet the district yard for that side (otherwise 5 ft from lines), max 10 ft tall, 12 ft per side and 100 sq ft, one per development site; satellite dishes stay 10 ft from the property line abutting the waterway. Sec. 47-19.2 (EE, satellite dish antennas). | Where it lives :: Unified Land Development Regulations Sec. 47-19.2 'Accessory buildings, structures and equipment, general' and Sec. 47-2.2 'Measurements'. | Guards (state rule) :: Florida Building Code, Residential, 8th Edition (2023), Sec. R312.1.1-R312.1.3: a guard is required on open sides of a walking surface located more than 30 inches above the floor or grade below at any point within 24 inches of the open edge; it must be at least 36 inches high; openings must not let a 4-inch sphere pass. No local guard amendment was found in this city's code.
source: City of Fort Lauderdale ULDR Sec. 47-19.2 (G, P, BB) and Sec. 47-2.2.S (ULDR Supp. 58 Update 2); Florida Building Code, Residential, 8th Ed. (2023) R312.1.1-R312.1.3 (ICC Digital Codes)

title: Checking a Marine Contractor in Fort Lauderdale
question: How do I check a marine contractor in Fort Lauderdale?
unit: licence + insurance kept current in LauderBuild
qualifier: Fort Lauderdale accepts building permit applications only from contractors holding a current certificate of competence and licence in their field (Code Sec. 9-27), and every licensed professional has to register and keep licence and insurance documents current in LauderBuild. Expired credentials block permits and even fee payments, and expired licences drop out of the public search - so a contractor you cannot find there is worth a phone call before you sign.
detail_rows: City registration :: Online only, through LauderBuild - not by email or post: a registration form, a state licence or county certificate of competency, liability insurance, and workers' comp or an exemption letter, with the City of Fort Lauderdale, as certificate holder - Contractors & Licensed Professionals page | Permits only to licensed contractors :: Applications for building permits are accepted only from contractors holding a current certificate of competence and license in their respective fields, apart from the exceptions in Secs. 9-28 and 9-29 - Code Sec. 9-27 | Business tax :: Before working, engaging in business or contracting in any listed classification, a contractor must pay any required local business tax and show the receipt on demand - Code Sec. 9-73 | Check them yourself :: In LauderBuild (aca-prod.accela.com/FTL) run a Licensed Professional Search, or Reports > LP License Status to see when their documents expire. Expired licences are not searchable at all | Minor work only :: The city lets non-licensed contractors register only for certain project types and minor construction work | County licence :: Broward's Building Code Division handles contractor licensing and enforcement under County Code Ch. 9 through the Central Examining Board of Construction Trades. County-licensed contractors, suspensions and revocations are checked by phone on 954-765-4400; complaints go to CLE-Complaint@broward.org | Marine cards are voluntary :: Broward lists its marine specialty, marine seawall, bulkhead, dock and pile-driving certificates under Division I (Voluntary), so a county card is not mandatory for marine work - Broward Contractor packet | State licence :: Search the company and the qualifier on DBPR's Verify a Licensee (myfloridalicense.com). A licence number starting with C is a state certification valid anywhere in Florida; one starting with R is a registration, good only where the holder met local competency rules - F.S. 489.105(8),(10) and the DBPR licensing page | Who may build a seawall or dock :: A certified general contractor's scope is unlimited (489.105(3)(a)). The state also certifies five marine specialties: marine specialty, marine seawall work, marine bulkhead work, marine dock work and marine pile driving - Rule 61G4-15.100(1)(b)-(f) | Workers' comp :: In construction a single employee makes coverage mandatory (440.02(20)(b)2). Up to three officers or LLC members owning at least 10% may file exemptions (440.02(18)(b)2), and the exemption certificate itself says it is not a DBPR licence (440.05(4)). Check it on the DWC data portal's Coverage and Exemptions search (dwcdataportal.fldfs.com) | Recovery fund :: For contracts signed on or after 1 July 2024 the Homeowners' Construction Recovery Fund pays at most $100,000 per claim against a Division I contractor (general, building, residential) and $30,000 against a Division II contractor, which includes the marine specialties; the lifetime caps are $2 million and $600,000 per licensee - 489.143(3),(6). Nothing is paid if the contractor was unlicensed when you signed - 489.141(2)(d) - and residential contracts over $2,500 must print the fund notice - 489.1425 | Deposits :: A contractor who takes more than 10% up front on residential work must apply for permits within 30 days and start within 90 days of the permits issuing, unless you agreed to longer in writing - 489.126(2)(a) | Three-day cancel :: If the deal was a home solicitation sale over $25 - signed away from the seller's place of business and not the result of your own request for specific goods or services - you can cancel in writing until midnight of the third business day; Sundays and federal holidays don't count - 501.021, 501.025 | Business tax is not a licence :: A contractor pays business tax where its permanent office is, and no other city or county may levy a business tax or an equivalent registration fee for temporary work there - 205.065

Admin. Code R. 61G4-15.100; DBPR Construction Industry page and Verify a Licensee; DFS Division of Workers' Compensation construction exemption page and data portal

title: Storm Prep for Fort Lauderdale Waterfront Owners
question: What are the storm and debris rules in Fort Lauderdale?
unit: no citywide boat-removal order
qualifier: Fort Lauderdale's code puts storm protection of a boat on its owner: a vessel at a municipal dock space must be protected by its owner once a hurricane warning is issued for Broward County. Boarding up openings for hurricane preparation during a watch or warning is carved out of the boarding-certificate rules, and a tidal flood barrier left in disrepair after a storm is a citable offence with fixed repair deadlines.
detail_rows: City dock space :: It is the responsibility of the owner of a vessel moored at any municipal dock space to protect the vessel upon the issuance of a hurricane warning for Broward County - Code Sec. 8-120 (Ord. C-91-69) | Boarding up :: Weather and hurricane preparation when a hurricane or tropical storm watch or warning has been issued by the National Weather Service is listed as an exception to the boarding-certificate requirement - Code Sec. 18-9(b) | Damaged seawall :: All property owners shall maintain a tidal flood barrier in good repair; one that lets tidal water flow unimpeded through it onto a neighbour or the right-of-way is presumed in disrepair. It is a citable offence: show progress within sixty (60) days of the citation and complete repairs within three hundred sixty-five (365) days - ULDR Sec. 47-19.13.D.2
source: City of Fort Lauderdale Code of Ordinances Secs. 8-120, 18-9; ULDR Sec. 47-19.13 (Municode)

title: Miami Beach Seawall Height Requirement
question: How high does a seawall have to be in Miami Beach?
unit: ft NAVD88
qualifier: Required for a new seawall, or an existing one undergoing substantial improvement. A wall being repaired below that threshold may be built to 4.0 ft NAVD88, but only if it is designed and constructed to accommodate a future 5.7 ft.
detail_rows: Interim elevation :: 4.0 ft NAVD88, allowed only for repairs that are less than substantial, and only if the wall is built to accommodate a future 5.7 ft. | What counts as substantial :: Repairs costing $500 or more per linear foot. Sec. 54-61, as amended by Ordinance 2025-4754 in July 2025. | Datum :: NAVD88 — the North American Vertical Datum of 1988. A figure quoted in MLW is not the same number. | Current ordinance :: 2025-4754, adopted 23 July 2025, amending Chapter 54, Article III. | The maintenance clock :: 60 days to show progress, 6 months to file permit applications with both the city and the county, 730 days to complete. | The fines :: $250 for a first offence, then $500 per day. | Two permits, not one :: City applications and Miami-Dade RER-DERM both have to be filed.

title: Seawall Permits in Miami Beach
question: Do I need a permit to repair a seawall in Miami Beach?
unit: Miami Beach building permit + county Class I
qualifier: Seawall work needs a Miami Beach building permit, and the city requires DERM approval as well. Most repairs also need a Miami-Dade DERM Class I permit, which the county requires for work in tidal waters in every city; sealing cracks and repairing pilasters are exempt. Repairs costing $500 or more per linear foot count as substantial and must bring the wall to 5.7 ft NAVD88.
detail_rows: City permit :: Seawalls are treated as special construction and need DERM approval in addition to a Building permit - Miami Beach Building Dept, Interactive Permit Guide | Applies to repairs :: The seawall article applies to building permits for new seawalls and for substantial improvements, including repair or rehabilitation; applicants submit an itemized cost breakdown of the seawall work. title: Miami Beach Flood Zone & Elevation Rules
question: What flood zone is Miami Beach in, and what does it require?
unit: above BFE; homes also at least 9.0 ft NGVD
qualifier: Miami Beach sets a minimum freeboard of 1 foot and lets owners build up to 5 feet above base flood elevation without the extra height counting against zoning. In A zones a home's lowest floor and equipment must also clear 9.0 ft NGVD (7.44 ft NAVD) and the crown of road or sidewalk plus 1 foot, whichever is highest. Improvements are added up over one year.

title: Dock Permits & Size Limits in Miami Beach
question: How big a dock can I build in Miami Beach?
unit: 15% (max 40 ft) on waterways over 100 ft wide
qualifier: In Miami Beach no dock, pile or other structure may reach more than 10% of a canal's width from the seawall. On waterways wider than 100 ft the limit is 15% of the width, never more than 40 ft, and on Biscayne Bay or any waterway over 1,000 ft wide a residential dock may reach up to 125 ft with state and county approval. A moored boat may not stick out past the same limits.
detail_rows: Projection :: Boat slips, docks, wharves, dolphin poles, mooring piles or structures of any kind may not extend more than 10% of the canal or waterway width at that spot, measured from the seawall (or the recorded plat line if there is no seawall) - City Code 66-113(a) | Wider waterways :: Over 100 ft wide: up to 15% of the width but never more than 40 ft - 66-113(a) | Biscayne Bay :: On Biscayne Bay or another waterway more than 1,000 ft wide, subject to state and county approval, up to 125 ft from a residentially zoned lot and up to 250 ft from a business-zoned lot - 66-113(a) | Boats :: No vessel may be docked or moored so that it projects beyond the permitted projection for the structures, and no mooring is allowed along either side of the walkway from the seawall to the dock - 66-113(a) | Beside WD-1 and WD-2 :: Any structure proposed more than 40 ft from a seawall next to the WD-1 or WD-2 waterway districts also needs conditional use approval from the Planning Board - 66-113(a) | Permit :: Building department permit, plus the state Internal Improvement Fund or any other agency with jurisdiction, and Army Corps approval where the lot abuts navigable waters - 66-113(b) | Lighting :: Any dock or pier reaching 20 ft or more into a city waterway needs a light at its tip, lit dusk to dawn and visible from all approaches; shorter structures need reflector signals at least 3 inches across - City Code 66-115(b) | Derelict docks :: A dock disintegrated beyond 50% of its original members must be replaced, removed or rebuilt, within ten days if it has sunk below mean high tide (Pelican Island between the Julia Tuttle and Venetian Causeways excepted) - 66-115(a) | Foam floats banned :: Unencapsulated expanded polystyrene floating docks, floating platforms and buoys are prohibited in all city waters - City Code 46-210 | Miami-Dade County Class I permit :: Any work in, on, over or upon tidal waters or bay bottom anywhere in Miami-Dade County, cities included, needs a county Class I permit - County Code 24-48.1(1)(a). title: Boat Lift Rules in Miami Beach
question: What are the boat lift rules in Miami Beach?

In single-family districts a davit or any marine structure must keep a 7.5-foot seaward side yard setback, and how far it may reach is set by the projection limits in the city's marine-structures chapter - 10% of the canal width, 15% (up to 40 feet) where the waterway is wider than 100 feet.

title: Checking a Marine Contractor in Miami Beach

title: Storm Prep for Miami Beach Waterfront Owners
question: What are the storm and debris rules in Miami Beach?
unit: minor-repair permit fee after a hurricane
qualifier: Miami Beach's fee schedule cuts the permit fee for minor repairs under $20,000 by 40% for three months after a hurricane event, though not for railing repairs, and repairs must be of substantially similar design. title: Dock Permits & Size Limits in Boca Raton
question: How big a dock can I build in Boca Raton?
unit: canals under 100 ft wide; 8 ft on wider waterways
qualifier: A Boca Raton dock may project only 6 ft into a canal or waterway narrower than 100 ft, or 8 ft into a wider one, measured from the property line, seawall or bulkhead, whichever is nearest the water. Longer reach comes from finger piers, which are allowed only in artificial coves, the Hillsboro and C-15 canals, the Intracoastal and Lakes Boca Raton, Wyman and Rogers. title: Boat Lift Rules in Boca Raton
question: What are the boat lift rules in Boca Raton?
unit: 25% of waterway or 20 ft (raised)
qualifier: Boca Raton has its own boat lift section. A lift is allowed in any waterway except the Boca Raton Inlet, may reach 25% of the canal width or 20 feet - measured with the lift fully raised - whichever is less, and must sit at least 10 feet from the neighbour's property line. Past 20% of the canal width only wood pilings may be used, and every lift must be designed by a state-registered engineer.

question: What are the storm and debris rules in Boca Raton?
unit: to apply after emergency repairs

title: Pompano Beach Seawall Height Requirement
question: How high does a seawall have to be in Pompano Beach?
unit: ft NAVD88 minimum

title: Seawall Permits in Pompano Beach
question: Do I need a permit to repair a seawall in Pompano Beach?
unit: city engineering + building permits + county license
qualifier: Yes. Pompano Beach makes it unlawful to construct or repair a seawall, cap or rip-rap without two city permits: an engineering permit from the City Engineer and a building permit from the City Building Official. Plans must come from a Florida-licensed engineer, and a wall below 5.0 ft NAVD88 that undergoes substantial repair must be raised to at least 5.0 ft (maximum 5 ft 10 in). Broward County also requires its own Environmental Resource License, often a general license for a repair in the same place.
detail_rows: City :: It is unlawful to construct, repair, erect or install seawalls, seawall caps, rip-rap or other flood barriers in city waterways without an engineering permit from the City Engineer and a building permit from the City Building Official; the qualified applicant must also seek Broward County, FDEP or SFWMD and Army Corps approvals unless exempt under s. 403.813, F.S. - Code s. 151.02(A). Plans by a Florida-licensed engineer, with as-built drawings and the engineer's completion certification before final acceptance - s. 151.02(C); the engineering permit fee is 4% of construction cost (minimum $100), plus a double fee if work starts before the permit - s. 151.02(D), (H). Substantial repair = work along more than 50% of the property's shoreline, or attached structures costing more than 50% of a barrier or raised cap as determined by the City Engineer - s. 151.01(B); barriers must be at least 5.0 ft and no more than 5 ft 10 in NAVD88, with lime rock rip-rap at the waterward face - s. 151.05(A), (F), (H). Engineering permits lapse if work does not start within 180 days or stops for 90 days; the City Engineer may grant one 180-day extension and no permit lasts over two years; re-inspections cost $30, four times that for repeat failures - s. 151.02(I), (L) If the applicant does not supply detailed cost information, the Building Official values the work from published construction cost data - s. 151.02(F); a permitted wall or other flood barrier destroyed by fire, casualty or force majeure may only be rebuilt to current rules - s. 151.02(A)(2) | Broward County :: Construction in regulated aquatic resources needs a county Environmental Resource License (ERL) - Broward County Code Sec. 27-333(a)(1). title: Boat Lift Rules in Pompano Beach
question: What are the boat lift rules in Pompano Beach?
unit: fully raised, from measurement reference line

title: Delray Beach Seawall Height Requirement
question: How high does a seawall have to be in Delray Beach?
unit: ft NAVD88 minimum
qualifier: Delray Beach sets one minimum in every flood zone, 4.2 ft NAVD88, and lets the maximum vary with your flood zone. The rule applies when a seawall is built, substantially repaired, or has fixed structures attached to it. Build below 5 ft and the wall must still be engineered so it can be extended to 5 ft later.
detail_rows: Minimum, every flood zone :: 4.2 ft NAVD88; Table 7.1.7(D) applies the same minimum to all three flood-zone rows. | When it applies :: New tidal flood barriers, substantial repair or rehabilitation of shorelines and shoreline structures, and installing fixed infrastructure attached to a barrier, such as docks or mooring structures. The applicability sentence ends with the words on the Intracoastal Waterway, so ask the city how it reads that for a canal lot. LDR 7.1.7(B). | Maximum, BFE 5.0 ft or higher :: The base flood elevation of the property, from the FEMA map. | Maximum, BFE of 4.0 ft :: 5 ft NAVD88. | Maximum, X zone outside the floodplain :: Must meet the definition of grade in Section 4.3.4(J)(2). | Build low, engineer high :: A wall built under 5 ft NAVD88 must be designed and constructed to accommodate a future extension to at least 5 ft. | What counts as substantial repair :: Work on more than 50% of the length of the structure, cap included, or any work changing the elevation along more than 50% of the length. Then the whole shoreline must meet the minimum. | Sellers must disclose :: Under LDR 7.1.7(D)(7), any contract to sell property in a tidally influenced area of Delray Beach, signed after 1 February 2022, must carry a tidal-flood-barrier disclosure in bold capitals of at least 14 point. | To get a permit :: A survey showing the seawall's location and elevation, plans sealed by a Florida registered engineer, and sign-off from the reviewing agencies first.
source: City of Delray Beach Land Development Regulations Sec. 7.1.7 and Table 7.1.7(D); Ordinance 23-21, adopted 11 January 2022

title: Seawall Permits in Delray Beach
question: Do I need a permit to repair a seawall in Delray Beach?
unit: building permit, engineer-sealed
qualifier: Yes. Delray Beach requires a building permit to build or alter a seawall, with plans sealed by a Florida engineer and approval from the other reviewing agencies before the permit issues. A substantial repair must meet the city's minimum elevation along the entire shoreline.
detail_rows: City :: 'The construction of a new seawall, or alteration of an existing seawall requires the issuance of a building permit'; the application needs a survey showing the wall's location and elevation, plans sealed by a Florida PE, and approval from the applicable reviewing agencies before the permit issues, which the applicant must obtain - LDR Sec. 7.1.7(E)(1)-(3) | Substantial repair :: Rip rap is not considered a seawall for this section - Sec. 7.1.7(C)(5); substantial repair is improvement to more than 50% of the length of the wall and cap, or an elevation change along more than 50% of it; the minimum then applies to the continuous seawall along the entire shoreline - Sec. 7.1.7(D)(6) | Elevation :: Minimum 4.2 ft NAVD88 in a floodplain with a BFE of 5.0 ft or more, maximum the property's BFE; walls built below 5 ft must be designed for a later extension to 5 ft NAVD88 - Sec. 7.1.7(D)(1) | Upkeep :: A cited owner must start repairs, such as hiring a contractor or submitting a building permit, show progress within 60 days and finish within 365 days - Code Sec. 100.04(C) (Ord. 22-21) | Disclosure :: The standard is sized for water levels through 2050, and sale contracts for tidally influenced property signed after 1 Feb 2022 must carry a 14-point bold disclosure - Sec. 7.1.7(A)(1), (D)(7). F.S.) | Federal :: A U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (Department of the Army) authorization is required for structures or work in or affecting navigable waters, unless exempt or covered by a nationwide or regional general permit - 33 CFR 322.3(a) (Rivers and Harbors Act s. 10)

title: Delray Beach Flood Zone & Elevation Rules
question: What flood zone is Delray Beach in, and what does it require?
unit: no extra city freeboard for buildings found
qualifier: Delray Beach keeps its flood rules in Chapter 10 of the land development regulations, uses the plain 50% substantial-improvement test, and lets owners add freeboard above the minimum under LDR Section 4.3.4(J)(2). title: Dock Permits & Size Limits in Delray Beach
question: How big a dock can I build in Delray Beach?
unit: max dock projection; piles up to 25% of waterway width
qualifier: Delray Beach rewrote its dock rules in January 2026. title: Storm Prep for Delray Beach Waterfront Owners
question: What are the storm and debris rules in Delray Beach?
unit: to show progress / finish a cited seawall
qualifier: Delray Beach makes failing to maintain or repair a needed seawall a public nuisance, with 60 days to show progress and 365 days to finish after notice. qualifier: Jupiter sets no minimum seawall height. It caps new bulkheads at the property's FEMA base flood elevation, and a bulkhead more than 3 ft above mean high water must be fully faced with riprap or mangroves.
detail_rows: Minimum :: None set in Sec. 27-2624 (Shoreline stabilization) | Maximum :: Top of new bulkhead must be at or below the property's required base flood elevation on current FEMA maps - Sec. 27-2624(8) | Exemptions to max :: Properties east of the Coastal Construction Control Line; Riverwalk properties where ADA slope cannot be met - Sec. 27-2624(8)a-b | Riprap trigger :: Top more than 3 ft above mean high water line requires 100% riprap/mangrove facing - Sec. 27-2624(1)c, (2)d | Location :: Replacement within 18 in. waterward of existing permitted bulkhead (one-time waterward move since 6/16/2015) - Sec. 27-2624(1)-(2) | Riprap placement :: Riprap must cover the bottom half of the bulkhead, sloped no steeper than 2:1, and may not reach more than 8 ft waterward of the mean high water line. Wood or other degradable walls must be removed - Sec. 27-2624(2)f, (2)h
source: Town of Jupiter Code of Ordinances, Ch. 27 Zoning, Art. XI Div. 25 Marine Facilities, Sec. 27-2624 (Supp. 24, online 10/2/2026)

title: Seawall Permits in Jupiter
question: Do I need a permit to repair a seawall in Jupiter?
unit: building permit (Marine Structure)
qualifier: Yes. Jupiter requires a town building permit for seawalls. title: Jupiter Flood Zone & Elevation Rules

title: Boat Lift Rules in Jupiter

title: Coral Gables Seawall Height Requirement
question: How high does a seawall have to be in Coral Gables?
unit: ft NGVD29 - a different datum again
qualifier: Coral Gables states its requirement in NGVD29, the old datum, while most of its neighbours use NAVD88. The two are not interchangeable and the city publishes no conversion. It is also the only city we have read where a seawall permit can be routed to a public hearing before the City Commission, and where the Board of Architects reviews the design.
detail_rows: The figure :: A minimum of 6 ft NGVD29, and the wall must structurally support 7.5 ft. Zoning Code Sec. 3-706. | Two numbers, two meanings :: The 6 ft is the elevation you build to. The 7.5 ft is structural capacity - what the wall must be able to carry. They are not the same requirement and should never be merged. | Mind the datum :: NGVD29, not NAVD88. The code states the datum explicitly and gives no conversion, and the offset between the two is local. Take it as written and get your datum from your survey. | No maximum :: Unlike Pompano Beach or Deerfield Beach, Coral Gables sets a floor and no ceiling. | Engineered and specified :: Plans must be designed by a Florida registered engineer, and the wall designed for loads imposed by saturated backfill. Reinforced, pre-stressed or gravity mass concrete - with block or native stone allowed only in water bodies west of LeJeune Road and north of Sunset Road. | The public hearing most people do not expect :: A seawall or bulkhead is a Class 2 waterfront permit, and the code requires a public hearing before the City Commission before it is approved, with 15 days' published notice and courtesy notice to riparian owners within 1,000 feet. The exceptions that waive the hearing cover mooring piles, residential docks and dock repair - not seawalls. Sec. 109-42(c) and (f). Confirm current practice with Public Works, because this is the code as written. | A biological survey :: Class 2 applications require a biological survey and ecological study. Sec. 109-42(b)(5)(e). | The Board of Architects :: Coral Gables reviews the look of the work. City Architect or Board of Architects approval is on the permit checklist, and the Building Official may not waive it. | The bond, correctly stated :: A performance bond set by the Public Works Director. The minimum is $1,000 or 25% of the estimated cost, whichever is lesser; the maximum is 100% of the estimated cost. It stays in force at least six months after the approved completion date. Sec. 109-42(e)(3). A separate refundable damage deposit may also be required. | Maintenance is enforceable :: It is unlawful to let a retaining wall between your property and a canal deteriorate to the point it encroaches or falls into the canal. Sec. 86-119(b). After notice you have 20 days to remedy or request a hearing, after which the city may do the work and lien the property at 6% interest. Secs. 86-120 to 86-123. The scheduled civil penalty for failure to maintain waterfront improvements is $400. | Recertification :: Any mooring structure ten years or older requires certification by a licensed engineer, and re-certification every five years after. Sec. 109-44(b). | Your dock is measured off the wall :: No dock more than 5 ft outward from the bank or the seawall, whichever is most restrictive. Sec. 3-702(A). Docks may not be covered or multi-level above grade. | Keep the channel clear :: 75 ft of navigable width south of US-1, 45 ft north of it, and 30 ft in the Mahi Canal. Sec. 3-702(C). | Two permits and a county stamp :: Public Works issues the Class 2 waterfront permit; Development Services runs the building permit; Miami-Dade DERM approval is required first and its stamp is required on revision re-submittals.

title: Storm Prep for Key Biscayne Waterfront Owners
question: What are the storm and debris rules in Key Biscayne?
unit: landscape debris must be gone

title: Deerfield Beach Seawall Height Requirement
question: How high does a seawall have to be in Deerfield Beach?
unit: ft NAVD88, and no more than 7.0
qualifier: Deerfield Beach adopted the county standard and then went further than any other Broward city we have read: it sets a ceiling as well as a floor, regulates how wide the cap may be, and bans retaining walls on top of it. If you are only checking the minimum, you are checking the easy half.
detail_rows: Minimum :: 5 ft NAVD88 for all new or substantially repaired tidal flood barriers. | The 2035 route :: An application before 1 January 2035 may be permitted at 4 ft NAVD88, if the barrier is designed and constructed to accommodate 5 ft NAVD88 by 1 January 2050. | Maximum :: 7 ft NAVD88, or the required finished grade elevation, whichever is higher. The county sets no ceiling at all, so this one is Deerfield's. | Cap width :: No less than 18 inches and no greater than 42 inches. | Retaining walls :: Prohibited on top of or over a seawall cap. | Riprap is required :: Natural limerock riprap, or approved habitat enhancement, at the waterward face. Placed from one foot above mean high water, at a slope no steeper than two horizontal to one vertical, with no reinforcing rods or protrusions and no filling gaps with concrete. | The whole shoreline :: A barrier undergoing substantial repair must be built along the property's entire shoreline, not only the failing section. | No gaps :: Barriers must adjoin immediately proximate barriers so far as practicable. | The clock :: 60 days to demonstrate progress after a notice, 365 days to complete. Tidal water crossing onto a neighbour or a right-of-way is a public nuisance and a citable offence. | What counts as substantial :: Work on more than 50% of the shoreline length, or an appurtenant structure costing more than 50% of a barrier along that shoreline. | Your dock is tied to it :: A dock may not exceed the height of the seawall, and where it is attached to the cap under sealed engineering it may sit no more than 6 inches above it. Minimum dock height with a seawall is 4 ft NAVD88. | Where it does not apply :: Oceanfront beaches and shorelines seaward of the Coastal Construction Control Line.
source: City of Deerfield Beach Land Development Code Sec. 98-87(d)(4)b, Docking and Mooring Facilities - Tidal Flood Barriers; Ord. 2022/003 and Ord. 2022/014; Broward County Code Ch. 39, Art. XXV, Sec. 39-407

title: Seawall Permits in Deerfield Beach
question: Do I need a permit to repair a seawall in Deerfield Beach?
unit: city permit + county license
qualifier: Yes. Deerfield Beach's land development code says no seawall or other shoreline structure may be built until the plans have the required approvals, and the city's Building Division, with plan review and inspections run by CAP Government, issues Florida Building Code permits. A substantial repair must meet the city's tidal flood barrier standard, including a cap 18 to 42 inches wide. Broward County also requires its own Environmental Resource License, often a general license for a repair in the same place.
detail_rows: City :: Docks and shoreline infrastructure, including seawalls and bulkheads, must meet city, county, state and district rules; no construction may occur until plans have the required approvals, and the owner is responsible for all other agencies' permits - LDC Sec. 98-87(d)(1)a. Substantial repair = work along more than 50% of the property's shoreline, or attached structures costing more than 50% of a tidal flood barrier - Sec. 98-87; such barriers need 5.0 ft NAVD88 (4.0 ft for applications before 1 Jan 2035), natural limerock rip-rap at the face, a top no higher than 7 ft NAVD88 or the required finished grade, a cap 18 to 42 inches wide, and no retaining wall on top of the cap - Sec. 98-87. The city says CAP Government handles Florida Building Code permit applications, plan approvals and inspections, with online submittal since 15 Dec 2025, and that through ePermitsOneStop customers can apply for city building permits and associated Broward County permits together - City Building Services page; inspection requests made by 3:00 PM are scheduled for the next business day. Dock decking may rest on a seawall cap only with sealed engineering showing it can carry the load, and then no more than six inches above the cap - Sec. 98-87(d)(1)g. | Broward County :: Construction in regulated aquatic resources needs a county Environmental Resource License (ERL) - Broward County Code Sec. 27-333(a)(1). Repairing an existing functional seawall no more than 1 ft waterward of its authorized location, or a new wall within 1 ft of the old wet face with the old wall left in place, qualifies for a general license (Sec. 27-336(a)(1)b.), as do refacing, crack filling, seepage holes and other minor repairs (n.) and raising the cap in the same footprint (o.); the code says a general license is issued within 10 days of a complete application - Sec. 27-336(a)(1) | State :: Restoring a seawall at its previous location, upland of it, or within 18 inches waterward is exempt from a state environmental resource permit; the exemption does not replace permission to use state-owned submerged land or county and city requirements, and does not cover chapter 161 coastal permits - s. 403.813(1), (1)(e), F.S. | Federal :: A U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (Department of the Army) authorization is required for structures or work in or affecting navigable waters, unless exempt or covered by a nationwide or regional general permit - 33 CFR 322.3(a) (Rivers and Harbors Act s. 10)

title: Deerfield Beach Flood Zone & Elevation Rules
question: What flood zone is Deerfield Beach in, and what does it require?
headline_answer: 18-24 in above road, never below FIRM
unit: residential first floor vs adjacent road centerline
qualifier: Deerfield Beach ties first-floor height to the road as well as the flood map: a home's first floor goes 18 to 24 inches above the centerline of the adjacent roadway, and never below the FEMA map elevation. Its floodplain chapter uses the plain 50% substantial-improvement test.
detail_rows: Floor vs road :: Residential first floor a minimum of 18 in and a maximum of 24 in above the centerline of the adjacent roadway; commercial/industrial 6-12 in - LDC Sec. 98-83. | Floor vs flood map :: In no case below the elevation established by the FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map - LDC Sec. 98-83. | Substantial improvement / damage :: 50 percent of market value, no cumulative period - LDC Ch. 90, Sec. 90-9. | FEMA flood map :: FEMA's Community Status Book (report dated 3 Oct 2026) lists Deerfield Beach as NFIP community 125101 with a current effective FIRM dated 31 Jul 2024. Zones are set parcel by parcel, so no single zone covers the whole city - check your own address. | NFIP history :: FEMA record: first flood hazard boundary map 10 Nov 1972; first FIRM 10 Nov 1972; regular NFIP program since 10 Nov 1972; entered CRS 1 Oct 1992. | Flood insurance discount :: CRS class 8 - 10% off NFIP premiums for policies in the Special Flood Hazard Area (class in effect 1 Oct 2020). | State minimum :: 2023 Florida Building Code, Residential R322.2.1 and R322.3.2 - lowest floor (A zones) or bottom of the lowest horizontal structural member (V and Coastal A zones) at BFE + 1 ft or the design flood elevation, whichever is higher. | Look up your zone :: Enter the address in FEMA's Flood Map Service Center (msc.fema.gov), the official public source for FIRMs; an elevation certificate shows how your floor compares with the BFE.

title: Dock Permits & Size Limits in Deerfield Beach
question: How big a dock can I build in Deerfield Beach?
unit: dock; dock + boat together max 25%
qualifier: On Deerfield Beach's seawalled canals a dock may reach 10% of the water body's width, and the dock, any mooring structure and the boat together may never take more than 25%. On the Intracoastal the dock limit is 20 ft or what the Army Corps permits, with an overall cap of 25% of the width or 30 ft. Boats must lie parallel to the seawall with no rafting.
detail_rows: Dock projection :: Seawalled tidal lots: 10% of the water body width; Intracoastal shoreline: 20 ft or as permitted by the Army Corps of Engineers; mangrove-fringe shorelines: 20% of the width - LDC 98-87(d)(3), Table A | Total projection :: Dock, mooring structure and vessel together may never exceed 25% of the water body's width - 98-87(d)(2)b. Table A caps Intracoastal projection at 25% of the Intracoastal width or 30 ft, whichever is more restrictive | Width measured :: Laterally across the water body; seawall to seawall where both banks are walled - 98-87(d)(1)j | Side setbacks :: Docks 5 ft from the bisecting lines (property lines extended at 90 degrees from the bulkhead); at canal dead ends and non-parallel waterfronts on lots under 100 ft, 5 ft or 10% of the waterfront lot line, whichever is less; boats 5 ft from each bisecting line - Table A, 98-87(d)(2)c | Height :: With a seawall, the dock may not be higher than the seawall and, if built before 2035, at least 4 ft NAVD88 designed to reach 5 ft NAVD88 by 1 January 2050; decking on the cap needs sealed engineering and may sit no more than 6 inches above it. Without a seawall, between 4 ft above mean low water and 5 ft above mean high water - 98-87(d)(1)e-g | Depth :: At least 4 ft of water at mean low water at the terminal end, unless a dock at the full allowed percentage reaches 4 ft within 5 ft of its end - 98-87(d)(1)d | Platform size :: Where there is no mangrove fringe, a terminal platform may be no wider than 8 ft in one dimension and no more than 160 sq ft - 98-87(d)(4)d | One dock :: One dock per single-family or two-family dwelling; a principal structure with a certificate of occupancy is required first - 98-87(d)(1)c,h | Boats :: Moored parallel to the seawall with no rafting; personal watercraft may sit perpendicular up to 16 ft or 25% of the width, whichever is less - 98-87(d)(2)a | Lifts :: Lots under 100 ft: one lift, 10 ft from the bisecting lines; 100 ft or more: up to two lifts, 25 ft from them - 98-87(d)(3)e | Dolphins :: None on waterways under 80 ft wide; 80-100 ft: up to 2, 25 ft or 25%, keeping a 50 ft clear channel; over 100 ft: 30 ft or 25%; 10 ft from bisecting lines; 6-8 ft above mean high water - 98-87(d)(3)f, Table B | Lighting :: Dock lights no higher than 48 inches above the decking, no red or green lights - 98-87(d)(4)a | Ladders :: One safety ladder to 2 ft below mean low water; two on docks over 50 ft long - 98-87(d)(1)k | Broward County license :: Work in the county's regulated aquatic resources, which include canals and tidal waters, needs a Broward County Environmental Resource License - County Code 27-332, 27-333(a)(1). A new dock, floating dock or other over-water structure of 500 sq ft or less, measured from the seawall's wet face at mean high water, with no dredging or filling beyond the pilings, qualifies for a general license issued within 10 days of a complete application - 27-336(a)(1)e. A county ordinance that sets minimum environmental-protection standards prevails over city ordinances - Broward County Charter Sec. 11.01 | State exemption :: A private, non-commercial dock on pilings with 1,000 sq ft or less of over-water surface (500 sq ft in Outstanding Florida Waters), and the only exempt dock along 65 ft of shoreline (or one per lot if the lot is narrower), needs no state environmental permit - Fla. Stat. 403.813(1)(b). The exemption does not grant permission to use state-owned submerged lands and does not override city or county rules - 403.813(1) | Federal :: Structures in navigable waters need a Department of the Army permit, general or individual - 33 CFR 322.3(a)

title: Boat Lift Rules in Deerfield Beach
question: What are the boat lift rules in Deerfield Beach?
headline_answer: Allowed; 1 lift under 100 ft frontage, 2 above
unit: 10 ft / 25 ft from bisecting lines
qualifier: Deerfield Beach ties the number of lifts to water frontage: one boat lift on a lot with less than 100 feet, set back 10 feet from the bisecting lines, and up to two on 100 feet or more, set back 25 feet. A lift platform holding up to three jet skis counts as one lift. Dock, lift and boat together may not take more than 25% of the water body, and any dock with a lift must have cleats or rings to tie the boat down in high wind.
detail_rows: How many and setback :: Frontage under 100 feet - one boat lift, 10 feet from the bisecting lines; 100 feet or more - up to two boat lifts, 25 feet from the bisecting lines - LDC Sec. 98-87(d)(3)e.1-2 | Jet skis :: Personal watercraft elevators and platforms holding up to three personal watercraft count as one boat lift - Sec. 98-87(d)(3)e.3 | Reach :: Docks, boat lifts and mooring structures may extend 25% of the canal width; on the Intracoastal, 25% of the width or 30 feet, whichever is more restrictive; nontidal lakes 101-199 feet wide, 25% or 25 feet; over 200 feet, 25% or 50 feet - Table A | Total footprint :: The dock, mooring structure and vessel together may never exceed 25% of the water body width - Sec. 98-87(d)(2)b | Tie-downs :: Docks with boat lifts, davits or similar lifting mechanisms must provide cleats, rings or similar points to tie the vessel down out of the water in high wind - Sec. 98-87(d)(1)m | Principal structure first :: No dock or mooring structure on a property without a principal structure with a certificate of occupancy - Sec. 98-87(d)(1)c | Definition :: A boat lift/davit is a manual, electronic or fuel-operated device fixed to the ground, seawall, finger pier or dock to lift watercraft clear of the water - Sec. 98-87(c) | Approvals :: Plans need approval from every agency with jurisdiction before construction, and the applicant must own the waterfront land or have the owner's consent - Sec. 98-87(d)(1)a-b | Broward County :: Boatlifts and davits are listed among the projects that qualify for a county general environmental resource license, which the code says is issued within ten days of a complete application - Broward County Code Sec. 27-336(a)(1)f. | State and federal :: Floating boat lifts and floating vessel platforms that meet s. 403.813(1)(s), F.S. title: Miami Seawall Height Requirement
question: How high does a seawall have to be in the City of Miami?
unit: ft NAVD88 (Miami River: 4 ft, built to rise 2 ft)
qualifier: Miami-Dade County sets no countywide seawall elevation, so the City of Miami sets its own. On tidally influenced and waterfront properties citywide, seawalls, bulkheads, living shorelines and other shoreline protection must be built to at least 6 ft NAVD88. The Miami River and its tributaries are the exception: 4 ft NAVD88, designed so the wall can be raised at least 2 ft more through 2070. City Code Sec. 29-89(a)(4).

Sec. 29-89(a)(4). | The Miami River :: Minimum 4 ft NAVD88 for new walls fronting the river or its tributaries, designed and built so they can be raised incrementally by at least 2 ft through 2070. Sec. 29-89(a)(4). | The raise plan :: A permit application must be accompanied by a plan for incremental improvements through 2070, with modification details and load calculations showing the wall can be raised at least 2 ft. Sec. 29-89(a)(4). | When it applies :: New construction, or when substantial improvements to a property are performed. Sec. 29-89(a)(4). | The 50% trigger :: A repair covering 50% or more of the wall's length, costing 50% or more of a new wall, or changing the elevation along 50% or more of its length must meet the standard for the length of the property. Sec. 29-89(a)(5). | Built to hold water :: Walls must be substantially impermeable, stopping water flowing through or over them while still relieving hydrostatic pressure from the land side. Sec. 29-89(a)(2). | The variance route :: An owner can ask the city manager's designee for a variance, for example an alternative construction method where an existing building stops the wall being raised, or to keep safe boat dockage at a single-family home, provided tidal water is still kept off neighbours and the right-of-way. title: Surfside Seawall Height Requirement
question: How high does a seawall have to be in Surfside?
unit: FEMA base flood elevation, max town DFE
qualifier: Surfside ties its seawall height to the FEMA flood map, not to a fixed number. Since Ordinance 23-1734 (14 March 2023), the top of a seawall on Biscayne Bay, Indian Creek or Point Lake must be at or above the base flood elevation on the FIRM, may not exceed the town's minimum design flood elevation, and must be built so at least two more feet can be added later. Code Sec. 90-63.4.
detail_rows: Minimum :: At or above the base flood elevation (BFE) on the applicable FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map, for every seawall fronting Biscayne Bay, Indian Creek and Point Lake. Surfside Code Sec. 90-63.4. | Maximum :: No higher than the town's minimum design flood elevation (DFE), which the code puts at approximately plus 8.5 NAVD as of the 2023 ordinance. Sec. 90-63.4(a). | Built to go higher :: The wall must be structurally designed and built to take at least two feet of additional elevation for projected sea level rise. Sec. 90-63.4(b). | When it applies :: A new seawall; repairs or renovations costing more than 50% of a new seawall; a new home; or renovations to an existing home exceeding 50% of the home's fair market value. Sec. 90-63.4(c). | The house can trigger the wall :: Building a new home, or renovating one past half its value, brings the seawall under this rule even when nobody planned to touch the wall. Sec. 90-63.4(c)(iii)-(iv). | Mind the datum :: Your BFE is read from the FIRM in the datum the map states, and the DFE cap is given in NAVD. title: Surfside Flood Zone & Elevation Rules
question: What flood zone is Surfside in, and what does it require?
unit: no extra town freeboard found

title: Bay Harbor Islands Seawall Height Requirement
question: How high does a seawall have to be in Bay Harbor Islands?
unit: ft MSL (mean sea level); optional up to 6.0 ft MSL on listed bay-facing lots
qualifier: The top of any seawall cap must be at 5.50 ft above mean sea level. Certain lots facing Biscayne Bay wave action may choose to go up to 6.0 ft above MSL. The code uses MSL, not NAVD88 or NGVD29.
detail_rows: Required height :: Elevation at top of any seawall cap shall be 5.50 ft above MSL - Bay Harbor Islands Code Sec. 23-12(10)(c) | Optional higher cap :: Lots 11-29 Blk 2; Lots 1-4 Blk 3; Lots 1-5 Blk 4; Lots 29-95 Blk 23; Tracts C-F (PB 46 Pg 5) may elect 6.0 ft above MSL - Sec. 23-12(10)(c) | Approval :: No seawall may be erected, constructed or repaired without written Town approval - Sec. 23-12(10) | Design :: Designed and certified by a registered engineer, built by licensed contractor - Sec. 23-12(10)(d) | Older low walls :: Existing seawalls built another way may stay as non-conforming structures and may continue to be repaired; the town strongly encourages raising them to the subsection (c) height and removing failed tie-backs - Sec. 23-12(10)(h) | How it must be built :: Reinforced concrete with a cap beam on concrete pilings driven to bedrock; rip-rap cannot replace a seawall, and all existing tie-backs come out when a wall is replaced - Sec. 23-12(10)(g)
source: Bay Harbor Islands Code of Ordinances Sec. 23-12(10)(c), (d), (g), (h) (Municode Supp. 10 Upd. 2)

title: Seawall Permits in Bay Harbor Islands
question: Do I need a permit to repair a seawall in Bay Harbor Islands?
unit: town building permit + written town approval + county Class I
qualifier: No seawall may be built or repaired in Bay Harbor Islands until the Town approves its location, design, materials and strength in writing, and the Town's permit list names seawall repairs. Most repairs also need a Miami-Dade DERM Class I permit, which the county requires for work in tidal waters in every city; sealing cracks and repairing pilasters are exempt.

title: Bay Harbor Islands Flood Zone & Elevation Rules
question: What flood zone is Bay Harbor Islands in, and what does it require?
unit: no extra town freeboard found

title: Dock Permits & Size Limits in Bay Harbor Islands
question: How big a dock can I build in Bay Harbor Islands?
unit: 15 ft on the Bay Harbor Waterway between the islands
qualifier: In Bay Harbor Islands a dock may extend no more than 25 ft beyond the outside face of the seawall cap, or 15 ft on the Bay Harbor Waterway between the east and west islands. Any part of a dock more than 8 ft out may be only 4 ft wide, docks may not be covered, and every dock must stay 10 ft from the projected side lines. Going beyond these limits takes a Town Council variance backed by a county environmental assessment.
detail_rows: Projection :: No dock more than 25 ft beyond the outside face of the seawall cap - Town Code 23-12 (dock provisions, (a)(iii)). On the Bay Harbor Waterway between the east and west islands (Block 2 lots 1-12, Block 3 lots 1-32, Block 23 lots 1-28 and 96-104) no more than 15 ft - (a)(iv) | Width :: A dock extending more than 8 ft beyond the seawall cap may be no more than 4 ft wide, with no obstructions - (a)(v) | Side setback :: No part of a dock nearer than 10 ft to the projected side lines (the code's wording is 'the sidelines of the dock') - (a)(vii) | Height :: The deck may be no higher than the seawall cap (or a retaining wall attached to it), except that a yard deck's material carried across the cap may reach 6.5 ft above mean sea level; the dock surface must be at least 5 ft above mean sea level unless Miami-Dade DERM or the Army Corps approves otherwise - (a)(i),(xi) | Seawall loading :: No dock may bear on the seawall or cap unless a licensed engineer certifies the added load is within the seawall's design - (a)(ii) | No covers :: No boathouse, dock building or dock cover - (a), (a)(vi) | Boats :: On the Bay Harbor Waterway no part of a vessel may extend more than 30 ft beyond the seawall cap; the Town may regulate the size and type of boats moored along its waters - 23-12 | Lifts and davits :: At least 10 ft from the projected side lines, no more than 25 ft beyond the seawall cap, self-supporting with no attachment to the seawall, no canopy, plans approved in writing by the town manager - 23-12(b) | Mooring piles :: No more than 40 ft beyond the seawall cap (30 ft on the Bay Harbor Waterway) and at least 7.5 ft from the projected side lot lines - 23-12(8) | Approval and variances :: Plans approved in writing by the town manager; Miami-Dade DERM may require changes for Biscayne Bay and Bay Harbor Waterway conditions, and any departure needs a Town Council variance with a DERM environmental assessment - (a)(viii),(x) | Miami-Dade County Class I permit :: Any work in, on, over or upon tidal waters or bay bottom anywhere in Miami-Dade County, cities included, needs a county Class I permit - County Code 24-48.1(1)(a). New boat slips at docks in tidal waters need at least 4 ft of water at mean low water; the depth rule does not apply to docks in bulkheaded artificial canals bordered by uplands on both sides, to lifts, davits and piles in slips at existing permitted docks, or to repair of existing legal docks with at least 3 ft of water - 24-48.3(3). A dock proposed beyond the boundaries in Sec. D-5(03)(2)(a) of the county Public Works Manual gets extra review factors - 24-48.3(1)(j) | State exemption :: A private, non-commercial dock on pilings with 1,000 sq ft or less of over-water surface (500 sq ft in Outstanding Florida Waters), and the only exempt dock along 65 ft of shoreline (or one per lot if the lot is narrower), needs no state environmental permit - Fla. Stat. 403.813(1)(b). title: Boat Lift Rules in Bay Harbor Islands
question: What are the boat lift rules in Bay Harbor Islands?
unit: 25 ft beyond seawall cap; 10 ft off side lines
qualifier: Bay Harbor Islands has a dedicated boat lift and davit rule. No part of a lift may extend more than 25 feet beyond the outside face of the seawall cap, the lift and the lifted boat must stay 10 feet from the projected side property lines, and the lift may not be fastened to or supported by the seawall. Covers and canopies are not permitted, and the town manager must approve the plans in writing.
detail_rows: Definition :: Any device used to raise or lower a boat or other water vehicle to or from the water surface - Code Sec. 23-12(6)(b)(i) | Side setback :: No part of the lift or davit, or of the watercraft on it, closer than 10 feet to the projected side property lines - Sec. 23-12(6)(b)(ii) | Reach :: No part of a boat lift or davit more than 25 feet beyond the outside face of the seawall cap - Sec. 23-12(6)(b)(iii) | Not on the seawall :: No attachment or fastening to the seawall or seawall cap; lifts and davits must be structurally self-supporting - Sec. 23-12(6)(b)(iv) | Covers :: No cover or canopy may be erected in connection with any boat lift or davit - Sec. 23-12(6)(b)(v) | Approval :: No boat lift or davit until the plans are approved in writing by the town manager - Sec. 23-12(6)(b)(vi) | Bay Harbor Waterway :: Docks between the east and west islands are limited to 15 feet and vessels to 30 feet beyond the seawall cap - Sec. 23-12(6)(a)(iv), (ix) | Miami-Dade County :: Any work in, on or over tidal waters needs a county permit from the Department (DERM). title: Waterfront Deck Rules in Bay Harbor Islands
question: What are the deck setback and railing rules in Bay Harbor Islands?
unit: from the seawall for water-side pools; pool decks 5 ft from side/rear lines
qualifier: Bay Harbor Islands lets a pool sit on the water side of a waterfront lot only if it is no more than 2 ft above finish grade and at least 5 ft from the seawall. No dock or deck may bear on the seawall or its cap unless a licensed engineer certifies the loads.
detail_rows: Water-side pools :: On waterfront lots, pools, hot tubs and spas on the side that abuts the water must not exceed 2 ft above finish grade and must not be closer than 5 ft to the seawall. Code Sec. 23-12. | Pool decks :: No part of a pool or spa deck closer than 5 ft to a side or rear lot line or in the minimum front setback; deck plans and a material sample need town manager or design review board approval. Sec. 23-12. | Loads on the seawall :: No dock or deck may bear weight on the seawall or seawall cap unless a licensed professional engineer presents vertical and lateral calculations. Sec. 23-12. | Open-air structures :: On West Island waterfront lots, canopies, thatched huts, cabanas and gazebos may come no closer than 5 ft to the lot line or the seawall, with design review approval. Sec. 23-12. | Block 23 waterfront rear setbacks :: Lots 29-95: 40 ft from the outside bulkhead wall; Lots 1-28 and 96-104: 25 ft. Sec. 23-11. | Guards (state rule) :: Florida Building Code, Residential, 8th Edition (2023), Sec. title: Storm Prep for Bay Harbor Islands Waterfront Owners
question: What are the storm and debris rules in Bay Harbor Islands?
unit: after a hurricane watch to empty dumpsters and clear yard debris
qualifier: Bay Harbor Islands gives landowners three hours after a hurricane watch is posted for Miami-Dade County to empty or cover dumpsters of construction debris and to remove or tie down yard debris and trash, and the rule stays in force until the all-clear. title: Storm Prep for Highland Beach Waterfront Owners
question: What are the storm and debris rules in Highland Beach?
unit: maximum fine for an unsecured job site
qualifier: Highland Beach requires construction materials to be secured on a hurricane watch, and roof tiles not yet fastened to be removed or secured before a warning; ignoring the building official can bring a stop-work order and a fine of up to $5,000 set by the Town Commission after the storm.
